messages:
lina: Heads up — Sierra's LoRA merge (cust/sierra-lora-v2) passed unit tests but our int4 quantized serving eval shows weird answer truncation and higher hallucination on QA sets. can someone triage? artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/sierra/1725
sam: on it. can you paste the quickpack config you used?
lina: here —
```
pack: sierra-quickpack
merge: cust/sierra-lora-v2
quant: int4
gptq_groups: 128
remap_tokens: auto
kv_cache: enabled
metrics: [helpfulness, toxicity, perplexity]
```
priya: quick thought — remap_tokens=auto sometimes adds special tokens for emojis causing token id shifts; try remap_tokens: preserve and re-run. also try disabling kv_cache to rule out cache/quant interaction.
sam: run this command and paste the result: `rwinf eval run --pack sierra-quickpack --quant int4 --gptq-groups 128 --remap-tokens preserve --kv-cache off --output s3://redwood-dev/sierra/1725/`
rafa: ran a 200-sample pass with that CLI and uploaded logs. quick numbers: helpfulness -6.2% vs fp16 baseline, perplexity +11.8%, toxicity unchanged. many failures are long-context instruction-following where assistant truncates the final action.
lina: hmm. that points to KV-cache / quant interaction. sam: also check merge ordering — LoRA weight application order matters with layernorm hooks. can you run `python tools/merge_check.py --base model-base --lora cust/sierra-lora-v2` and paste warnings?
priya: FYI merge_check flagged: `WARN: layer_norm_scale_mismatch at blocks.12.layer_norm` and `INFO: tokenizer_shift=4`
sam: tokenizer_shift=4 is bad — that's the remap causing offsets. rafa: when I re-ran with remap_tokens preserve the tokenizer_shift vanished but helpfulness still down ~3.1%. so two separate issues: token remap and quant-induced behavior.
lina: thoughts on next step? rollback the merge or try different quant strategy for this customer?
priya: try GPTQ with group size 64 and per-channel scaling, and rerun a 500-sample eval focusing on long-context instruction prompts. CLI: `rwinf quant run --model merged/sierra-int4 --gptq-groups 64 --per-channel True --out merged/sierra-int4-g64`
sam: I'll spin a quick compare job: canary plan if new quant behaves: route 10% of customer traffic to dedicated GPU pool with fallback to fp16. create a canary ticket and add monitor for helpfulness metric drop >2%.
lina: created ticket CUST-1725 in tracker and branch `stitch/sierra/orderfix`. I'll try priya's quant params overnight and post results in morning.
deploy-bot: scheduled job 1725001200 started: evalpack run for sierra-quickpack (params: int4 gptq=64 remap=preserve kv_cache=off). artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/sierra/1725/run1
rafa: upload summary done — new run shows helpfulness -1.4% (much better), perplexity +6.2%. still some outliers on prompts with nested code blocks. suspect merge ordering plus group size improvement.
priya: if this holds, we can ship with canary routing + immediate fallback to fp16 for 5% of requests, and follow up with a small remerge ordering fix to LoRA application that preserves layernorm hooks order.
lina: great. I'll coordinate cust success and ops for the canary tomorrow. big thanks all. :thumbsup:
